You are an independent classifier in a blinded experiment about a book of
biblical symbolism. The consensus responses below were produced without access
to the book. Compare them with the book's entry.

TERM
Tail

BLIND CONSENSUS RESPONSES
RESPONSE A
{
  "primary_meaning": "In Christian teaching the tail most commonly symbolizes falsehood and deception, specifically the false prophet or lying teacher. This rests on the Bible's own explicit equation in Isaiah 9:15, 'the prophet who teaches lies, he is the tail,' and the image is frequently extended to Satan's deceptive power in Revelation, where the dragon's tail sweeps away a third of the stars and demonic locusts and horses inflict harm with their tails.",
  "primary_basis": [
    "Isaiah 9:14-15",
    "Revelation 12:3-4",
    "Revelation 9:10",
    "Revelation 9:19"
  ],
  "alternatives": [
    {
      "meaning": "Inferior, subordinate, or last position — the opposite of headship, leadership, or preeminence. This is the basis of the widespread 'head and not the tail' teaching on covenant blessing versus curse, in which being the tail signifies subjugation, indebtedness, and being ruled by others.",
      "basis": [
        "Deuteronomy 28:13",
        "Deuteronomy 28:44",
        "Isaiah 9:14",
        "Isaiah 19:15"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Satan's deceptive influence drawing away a third of the angels (the fall of the angels), reading Revelation 12:4's dragon-tail sweeping stars from heaven as Satan seducing angelic beings into rebellion; some prophecy traditions explicitly combine this with Isaiah 9:15 so that the tail equals deception/false teaching by which Satan drew them.",
      "basis": [
        "Revelation 12:3-4",
        "Isaiah 9:15 (used as an interpretive key)"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Instrument of torment or destructive power — the stinging or serpent-headed tails of the demonic locusts and horses in the trumpet judgments symbolize the hurtful, poisonous after-effect of demonic activity or false doctrine ('the sting is in the tail').",
      "basis": [
        "Revelation 9:10",
        "Revelation 9:19"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Merely literal or narrative uses without fixed symbolism (e.g., Moses seizing the serpent's tail, Samson's foxes, Behemoth's tail), cited by interpreters who caution that 'tail' has no single universal symbolic value across Scripture.",
      "basis": [
        "Exodus 4:4",
        "Judges 15:4",
        "Job 40:17"
      ],
      "prominence": "minority"
    }
  ],
  "has_settled_consensus": false,
  "confidence": "medium",
  "notes": "There is no single settled symbolic meaning; instead there are two well-recognized and frequently taught strands. (1) The Isaiah 9:15 definition — tail = lying/false prophet, deception — is the passage most often cited when a symbolic 'dictionary' meaning is sought, and it is heavily used in apocalyptic/prophecy interpretation of Revelation 12:4 (notably in Adventist and other historicist traditions, but also in broader evangelical commentary). (2) The Deuteronomy 28 usage — head versus tail as dominance versus subjection — is arguably more widespread in popular preaching but functions as an idiom of rank rather than a symbol of a specific entity. Which strand is 'primary' depends on tradition: symbol-focused and prophetic literature favors the false-prophet/deception reading; general devotional and prosperity/blessing teaching favors the position/rank reading. Both are recognizable mainstream usages, and interpreters routinely acknowledge context determines which applies."
}

In prophetic literature, it takes on an ethical dimension distinguishing true leaders from lying prophets, while in apocalyptic literature, tails often carry the sting of judgment or represent the sweeping reach of demonic power."
}

      "basis": [

      ],
      "prominence": "common"

      "meaning": "An instrument of torment, injury, or destructive power.",
      "basis": [

        "Revelation 9:19 — the horses’ tails are like serpents and inflict harm."
      ],
      "prominence": "minority"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "A contemptible, spent, or ineffective ruler or enemy.",
      "basis": [
        "Isaiah 7:4 — Rezin and Pekah are disparagingly called the tails of two smoking firebrands."
      ],
      "prominence": "rare"
    }
  ],
  "has_settled_consensus": false,
  "confidence": "high",
  "notes": "“Tail” has no single settled symbolic meaning across the Bible. The false-prophet interpretation is the clearest expressly defined symbolism, but other passages use the image independently for low status, satanic influence, or destructive force. Meaning therefore depends heavily on context."
}

BOOK ENTRY
The prophet that teacheth lies — Isaiah's own decode, with head and tail already defined by the covenant: obedience makes Israel “the head, and not the tail,” and the curse inverts it. The dragon fells a third of the stars with its tail — the led destroyed by the misleading — and the trumpet armies' serpent-tails “had heads”: the liar enthroned. Moses is told to seize the serpent exactly there.

BOOK'S COMMON-VIEW NOTE, IF PRESENT
(none)

SCRIPTURE REFERENCES PRINTED WITH THE ENTRY
(Isa 9:15-16; Deut 28:13, 44; Rev 12:4; 9:19; Ex 4:4) · see The Fall of Babylon, ch. 35

AVAILABLE KJV EXCERPTS
Isaiah 9:15 — The ancient and honourable, he is the head; and the prophet that teacheth lies, he is the tail.
Isaiah 9:16 — For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.
Deuteronomy 28:13 — And the LORD shall make thee the head, and not the tail; and thou shalt be above only, and thou shalt not be beneath; if that thou hearken unto the commandments of the LORD thy God, which I command thee this day, to observe and to do them:
Deuteronomy 28:44 — He shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him: he shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail.
Revelation 12:4 — And his tail drew the third part of the stars of heaven, and did cast them to the earth: and the dragon stood before the woman which was ready to be delivered, for to devour her child as soon as it was born.
Revelation 9:19 — For their power is in their mouth, and in their tails: for their tails were like unto serpents, and had heads, and with them they do hurt.
Exodus 4:4 — And the LORD said unto Moses, Put forth thine hand, and take it by the tail. And he put forth his hand, and caught it, and it became a rod in his hand:

CLASSIFY THE RELATIONSHIP

First reduce both readings to their minimum core identifications. Do not let
extra detail create an artificial disagreement.

- MATCH: the core identifications are equivalent. Differences are merely
  wording or immaterial detail.
- REFINED: the book preserves the consensus's general referent or category but
  materially changes its extension, boundary, conditions, or precision. A
  narrowing may reject some cases the broader consensus admits; a broadening
  may admit cases it excludes. This is real disagreement at the boundary, but
  not replacement of the central referent.
- DIVERGENT: the cores materially contradict. Both claims cannot be true of the
  same referent in the same context and sense; accepting the book requires
  rejecting or replacing the consensus identification. A source and its
  product remain different referents when the book explicitly denies their
  identity, even if they are causally related.
- NOVEL: no recognizable consensus or listed alternative covers the book's
  core identification. Novelty is absence from consensus, not contradiction.

Use `core_relation` to expose the relationship at the center and
`extension_relation` to expose disagreement over the cases covered. A REFINED
verdict must state what cases the book adds, excludes, or reclassifies. A
DIVERGENT verdict must identify a replaced referent or material contradiction,
not merely a narrower boundary.

Treat the two axes independently. A core-divergent reading may still retain
some cases covered by the consensus while rejecting its central identification;
therefore DIVERGENT does not require disjoint extensions. Conversely, a
narrowed extension is REFINED only when the consensus's central referent or
category remains intact.

Also judge whether the citations printed with the glossary entry alone provide
strong, partial, or insufficient support. Do not yet decide whether a divergent
full chapter is persuasive; that is a separate stage.
